title: Gravitation
subtitle: Zero-to-JEE-Advanced Visual Textbook: Newton's Law of Gravitation, Shell Theorem, Variation of g (Altitude, Depth, Earth Rotation), Gravitational Field & Potential, Escape Velocity, Satellites & Kepler's Laws
introduction:
💡 First-Time Reader Intuition: Why Do Apples Fall and Planets Orbit?

In our everyday lives, gravity is simply the downward force that keeps us anchored to the ground. But in the 17th century, Sir Isaac Newton made one of the greatest unifications in human history: he realized that the exact same force pulling an apple toward the Earth (Gravity) is what keeps the Moon in orbit around the Earth, and the Earth in orbit around the Sun!

Universal Gravitation:
Every single particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

topics.title: Newton's Law of Gravitation & The Shell Theorem (Gravitational Force of Hollow & Solid Spheres)
topics.theoryHtml:
1.1 Newton's Law of Gravitation Vector Form
$$\vec{F}_{12} = -\frac{G m_1 m_2}{r^2} \hat{r}_{12}$$

Where $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$ is the Universal Gravitational Constant. The minus sign indicates that the gravitational force is strictly attractive.

1.2 Newton's Shell Theorem (Crucial for Earth & Planet Problems)
Position of Test Mass ($m$)Gravitational Force Inside / Outside a Uniform Hollow ShellGravitational Force Inside / Outside a Uniform Solid Sphere
Outside ($r > R$)Acts as if all mass $M$ is concentrated at the center: $F = \frac{GMm}{r^2}$Acts as if all mass $M$ is concentrated at the center: $F = \frac{GMm}{r^2}$
Inside ($r < R$)Zero! ($F = 0$) A test mass inside a hollow shell feels no net gravitational force.Proportional to distance from center: $F = \frac{GMm}{R^3}r$
topics.derivationHtml:
Why Gravity Inside a Solid Sphere Proportional to r

For $r < R$, only the enclosed mass $M_{\text{enclosed}} = M\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^3$ exerts force. Thus $F = \frac{G(M_{\text{enclosed}})m}{r^2} = \frac{GMm}{R^3}r$.

topics.jeeTraps: • Trap (Shell Theorem Inside): Do not forget that inside a hollow shell, the gravitational force is strictly zero.

topics.title: Variation of Acceleration Due to Gravity g (Altitude, Depth, Earth's Rotation & Shape)
topics.theoryHtml:
2.1 Variation with Altitude ($h$), Depth ($d$) & Latitude ($\lambda$)
$$\text{1. Altitude } (h): \quad g' = \frac{GM}{(R+h)^2} \approx g\left(1 - \frac{2h}{R}\right) \quad (\text{when } h \ll R)$$
$$\text{2. Depth } (d): \quad g' = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)$$
$$\text{3. Rotation of Earth at Latitude } \lambda: \quad g' = g - R\omega^2\cos^2\lambda$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Derivation of Depth Formula

$g' = \frac{G M_{\text{enclosed}}}{(R-d)^2} = \frac{G M (R-d)^3 / R^3}{(R-d)^2} = \frac{GM}{R^2}\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right) = g\left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)$.
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 190' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='190' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><path d='M 50 160 L 340 50 L 630 160' fill='none' stroke='#00e676' stroke-width='3'/><text x='340' y='40' fill='#00e676' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Maximum g at Surface (r = R)</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap (Binomial limit): Never use $g(1 - 2h/R)$ when $h$ is comparable to $R$.

topics.title: Gravitational Field, Potential Energy, Gravitational Potential & Escape Velocity
topics.theoryHtml:
3.1 Potential & Escape Speed Formulae
$$\text{Potential Energy:} \quad U = -\frac{GMm}{r} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \text{Gravitational Potential:} \quad V = -\frac{GM}{r}$$
$$\text{Escape Velocity from Planet Surface:} \quad \boxed{v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{2gR} \approx 11.2\text{ km/s (Earth)}}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Derivation of Escape Velocity

Total mechanical energy $E = \frac{1}{2}mv_e^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = 0 \implies v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$.
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 190' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='190' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><path d='M 50 40 Q 340 180 630 40' fill='none' stroke='#ff0055' stroke-width='3'/><text x='340' y='30' fill='#ff0055' font-size='12' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Gravitational Potential Well U(r) = −GMm / r</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Escape velocity is independent of the mass of the projectile!

topics.title: Satellite Motion: Orbital Speed, Total Energy, Binding Energy & Kepler's Three Laws
topics.theoryHtml:
4.1 Orbital Speed, Period & Energy of a Satellite
$$\text{Orbital Speed } (v_o): \quad \boxed{v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}} = \frac{v_e}{\sqrt{2}}}$$
$$\text{Orbital Period } (T): \quad \boxed{T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{r^3}{GM}}}$$
$$\text{Total Energy of Satellite:} \quad E = K + U = \frac{GMm}{2r} - \frac{GMm}{r} = \boxed{-\frac{GMm}{2r}}$$
4.2 Kepler's Three Laws of Planetary Motion
LawStatementFormula
1. Law of OrbitsAll planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun at one focus.Ellipse geometry
2. Law of AreasA planet-Sun line sweeps out equal areas in equal time intervals (Conservation of Angular Momentum!).$\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{L}{2m} = \text{constant}$
3. Law of PeriodsThe square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis.$T^2 \propto r^3$
topics.derivationHtml:
Derivation of Kepler's Third Law ($T^2 \propto r^3$):

$$\frac{mv_o^2}{r} = \frac{GMm}{r^2} \implies v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$$

Since $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v_o}$, squaring both sides yields $T^2 = \frac{4\pi^2}{GM}r^3 \implies T^2 \propto r^3$.

summary:
• Force: $F = \frac{GMm}{r^2}$.
  • Gravity Variation: $g' = g(1 - 2h/R)$ or $g(1 - d/R)$.
  • Escape Speed: $v_e = \sqrt{2gR}$.
  • Kepler: $T^2 \propto r^3$.
